info.name: Venny I/O
info.description:
# Venny I/O

Venny I/O is a cartridge-based REST API for building modular application experiences on a shared platform runtime. The collection is organized by domain so a development team can understand which cartridge owns each API surface and where a resource belongs.

## How to read this collection

Top-level folders represent Venny I/O domains or cartridges. Resource folders underneath each domain map to database-backed endpoint families. Most resource families follow the same REST pattern:

- `GET /resource` — list records
- `GET /resource/:id` — retrieve one record
- `POST /resource` — create a record
- `PATCH /resource/:id` — update a record
- `DELETE /resource/:id` — archive a record

## Authentication

Protected endpoints use {{bearer_token_0b1z}}:

`Authorization: Bearer {{api_key}}`

The Bearer key should identify the active app/tenant. In production, normal clients should not choose `created_for_app_id`; tenant ownership should be derived by the API from the authenticated key.

## Standard response envelope

Responses should follow the Venny I/O envelope:

```json
{
  "status": "200",
  "success": true,
  "message": "resource retrieved successfully",
  "data": {}
}
```

Collection responses should return records inside `data.items` and pagination details inside `data.pagination`.

## Pagination

Collection endpoints should support:

- `page`
- `per_page`
- `sort`
- `direction`

Example:

`GET /contacts?page=1&per_page=25&sort=time_started&direction=desc`

## Soft-delete behavior

`DELETE` requests should archive records rather than hard-delete them unless a specific endpoint explicitly documents otherwise. The common archive pattern is `status = archived` and `active = 0`.

## Development note

Use the collection variables for IDs created during testing. A common development flow is to create a parent record first, save its ID to a collection variable, then use that variable in related requests.


## Chatio user-session header

Chat endpoints require the app Bearer key and an active signed-in user session:

`X-Venny-Session-Id: {{session_id}}`

This lets the API enforce participant-level access instead of relying on the React UI to filter records.


## Account registration and session-scoped account settings

`POST /sign-up` now creates three records in one transaction: `persons`, `users`, and `profiles`. The `users` record owns login credentials, the `persons` record owns personal information, and the `profiles` record owns public/social metadata.

Browser account settings should use the Account facade endpoints instead of directly updating `/persons`, `/users`, or `/profiles`. Account endpoints require `X-Venny-Session-Id` and always derive the current user from the active session. Request bodies cannot select another user.

## Updates signup capture

`POST /sign-up-for-updates` creates a duplicate-allowed CRM `contacts` record from the submitted fields. Email is required. Name and phone are optional. The request must include a source view through `view`, `source_view`, `route`, or `contact_source.view`.

item.description:
# Platform

Core runtime and administrative primitives for Venny I/O.

## Owns

- apps
- keys
- cartridges
- installations
- steps
- windows
- sessions

## Purpose

Platform endpoints support app registration, API key management, cartridge discovery, setup workflows, rate-limit windows, and session records.

## Boundary

Domain cartridges should not duplicate platform responsibilities. Platform is the shared runtime layer that other cartridges build on top of.

item.name: Identity
item.description:
# Identity

Identity primitives for people, users, and public or private profiles.

## Owns

- persons
- users
- profiles

## Purpose

Identity endpoints support person records, application users, and profile records that other cartridges can reference.

## Boundary

Identity should not own CRM-specific contacts, commerce customers, messages, posts, or tenant/app registration.

item.description:
# Account

Session-scoped account settings facade. The UI should call these endpoints for account settings instead of directly calling `/persons`, `/users`, or `/profiles`.

## Requires

- `Authorization: Bearer {{api_key}}`
- `X-Venny-Session-Id: {{session_id}}`

## Owns no tables

Account is a facade over Identity tables and sessions. It safely aggregates and updates `persons`, `users`, and `profiles` for the active session user only.

item.description:
# CMS

Content and asset metadata management for Venny I/O experiences.

## Owns

- content
- assets

## Purpose

CMS endpoints manage structured content blocks, pages, copy, metadata, and asset records used by application experiences.

## Boundary

CMS stores content and asset metadata. Binary upload, storage-provider signing, and file transfer should live in integration cartridges.

item.description:
# CRM

Customer relationship management primitives.

## Owns

- contacts
- companies
- deals
- pipelines
- stages
- activities
- tasks
- notes
- tags

## Purpose

CRM endpoints manage relationship, sales, pipeline, activity, task, note, and tagging records for the authenticated app.

## Boundary

CRM should not own platform users, public profiles, storefront products, commerce orders, chat messages, or delivery-provider execution.

item.name: Communications
item.description:
# Communications

Communication orchestration and delivery metadata.

## Owns

- communications
- deliveries

## Purpose

Communications endpoints record outbound or inbound communication intent, recipients, templates, delivery metadata, and processing status.

## Boundary

Provider-specific sending should live in integration cartridges such as email, SMS, or notification-provider integrations. Chat threads and messages belong to the Chat cartridge.

item.description: Chatio facade endpoints that sit on top of /threads and /messages.

# Chat

Conversation primitives for thread and message records.

## Owns

- threads
- messages

## Purpose

Chat endpoints manage conversations, participants, message bodies, message metadata, attachments, and read state.

## Boundary

Chat should not own communications delivery records, provider sending logic, reactions, comments, or CRM activity history.

item.description:
# Posts

Post records for application timelines, feeds, updates, or object-level publishing.

## Owns

- posts

## Purpose

Posts endpoints manage authored content records that can be attached to users, profiles, objects, or other parent records.

## Boundary

Posts should not own comments, acknowledgements, relationships, profiles, or asset upload behavior.

item.name: Reactions
item.description:
# Reactions

Lightweight response primitives for object-level feedback and discussion.

## Owns

- acknowledgements
- comments

## Purpose

Reactions endpoints allow users or actors to acknowledge objects and add comments to posts, records, or parent objects.

## Boundary

Reactions should not own posts, threads, messages, followships, groups, or generic relationship records.

item.name: Relationships

request.description: Chatio reference lookup request. Returns followship records sent by one user.
Chatio reference lookup request. Returns followship records received by one user.
Chatio reference lookup request. Returns accepted followship records.

item.description:
# Relationships

Relationship primitives for follows and groups.

## Owns

- followships
- groups

## Purpose

Relationships endpoints manage follow/request status between actors and group records with participants, visibility, and group metadata.

## Boundary

Relationships should not own user identity, profile data, posts, comments, messages, or CRM associations.

item.description:
# Commerce

Transactional commerce records.

## Owns

- transactions
- orders
- coupons
- customers

## Purpose

Commerce endpoints manage order records, customer records, coupon definitions, and transaction metadata.

## Boundary

Commerce handles records and state. Payment-provider execution, checkout provider calls, settlement, and webhooks should live in integration cartridges.

item.description:
# Storefront

Catalog and merchandising records for public or private storefront experiences.

## Owns

- catalogs
- categories
- products
- items

## Purpose

Storefront endpoints manage catalog structure, product metadata, categories, item records, pricing, visibility, inventory-related fields, and merchandising content.

## Boundary

Storefront should not own customers, orders, coupons, transactions, payment execution, fulfillment, or shipping logic.
